top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) rests on one identifiable invention, the magic-wavelength lattice that cancels the clock-transition light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once. It is reproduced independently near 1e-18 in several laboratories, already yields new tests (millimetre-scale redshift, constants), and has the cleanest two-name credit on the slate. The main risk, overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes, is answerable by a citation naming the lattice scheme. P002 is a mature, conceptually important second choice, but its credit leaves out Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Hasan and Fu-Moore, and it sits near the 2016 prize. Either award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Possible but weak connections from profile: a research stay in John Hall's laboratory (Hall is a mentor of the clock/comb field in which Ye worked) and Lund atomic-physics ties to precision spectroscopy; no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye is documented.
